newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-ALDRIDGE RECALLED TO IRELAND WORLD CUP SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALDRIDGE RECALLED TO IRELAND WORLD CUP SQUAD.

text.p: Veteran Tranmere player-manager John Aldridge has been recalled to the Republic of Ireland squad for the World Cup qualifying tie against Macedonia at Lansdowne Road in Dublin on October 9.

But Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane faces the disappointing prospect of missing his return to the international scene through injury having been included in manager Mick McCarthy's original selection.
And there is still no room for Paul McGrath, although McCarthy has made it clear that the Aston Villa defender will come back into the reckoning if he can get regular first-team football.
Aldridge could win his 69th cap against the Macedonians. The 38-year-old striker has so far scored 19 international goals, just one short of Frank Stapleton's Irish record.
"John has been scoring goals for his club and that is good enough for me, especially with Niall Quinn and Jon Goodman injured," said McCarthy.
Keane has not played for his country since being sent off in the dying seconds of a 2-0 defeat by Russia in a friendly in Dublin last March.
Injuries, suspensions and a much publicised decision not to play in end-of-season friendlies in America means that the Old Trafford star has missed the Republic's last eight internationals.
In the likely absence of Keane, McCarthy may use Jason McAteer in his starting line-up. The Liverpool man missed last month's triumph in Liechtenstein as he suffered a virus on the day of the game.
